specification.problem: Characterize lazy quantum walks (Childs' construction): their n-th moment scaling O(t^n), the concentration interval of the lazy walk with a DFT coin compared with the Hadamard walk, and a new occupancy number/rate measure showing higher occupancy than normal quantum, classical and lazy classical walks.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite instance of a 1D lazy discrete-time quantum walk with explicit coin. The abstract gives only qualitative claims, so the exact lazy-walk operator and occupancy definitions are not given and remain assumed or missing. Only the moment scaling and normalization are formalized.

symbols.meaning: n-th moment of the position probability distribution after t steps
probability of finding the walker at position x after t steps

equations.label: Moment scaling
equations.description: The n-th moment of the lazy quantum walk distribution scales as t^n, as for normal quantum walks.
equations.abstract_quote: lazy quantum walks have $O(t^{n})$ order of the n-th moment of the corresponding probability distribution
equations.justification: Moment definition is standard; the scaling is stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Moment taken as the sum over x of x^n P(x,t)

equations.label: Probability normalization
equations.description: The position distribution is normalized at every step.

registers.name: coin
registers.size: 2 qubits (4-dim, for DFT coin) or 1 qubit; assumed
registers.role: Coin/laziness degree of freedom; the extra stay direction is encoded here

registers.name: position
registers.size: ceil(log2(2T+1)) qubits for T steps; assumed
registers.role: Walker position on a line (cyclic finite register)

specification.initial_state: Assumed: position |0>, coin in a fixed basis state, e.g. |0>; the paper's initial state is not given in the abstract.

steps.description: Prepare position at the origin and the coin in the assumed initial state.
Apply the coin operator (Hadamard or DFT) to the coin register.
Apply a conditional shift moving left, right, or staying (lazy) depending on coin state.
Repeat the coin and shift for t steps, then read the distribution P(x,t) and its moments.

specification.measurement: Measure the position register in the computational basis at step t, repeated over many runs to estimate P(x,t) (assumed; not stated in the abstract).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute moments M_n(t) and the concentration interval from the estimated P(x,t); occupancy number/rate cannot be computed since the definitions are missing.
assumptions: The 1D line walk is the setting.
Lazy walk is modeled as a coin with a stay direction (assumed); register sizes are assumed.
Measurement in the position basis with repeated runs is assumed.
Measurement is a computational-basis position readout with repeated runs.
missing_information: Exact lazy walk operator and laziness parameter
Definition of occupancy number and occupancy rate
DFT coin dimension and initial coin state
Quantitative concentration interval for the DFT lazy walk
